subject: physics
question_text: Write the SI unit and the dimensional formula of impulse. Is impulse the same physical quantity as momentum?

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Unit and dimensions
lines: Impulse J = force × time of contact.
steps.why: Multiplying force by time removes one power of T from [M L T⁻²], which is exactly the dimensions of momentum.
common_mistakes: Writing the unit as N/s instead of N s.

recall.must_convey: That the SI unit of impulse is newton second and its dimensional formula is M L T to the minus one.
accept: M L T to the power minus one
reject: they are not the same quantity

steps.memory_tip: [M L T⁻¹] reads as mass × velocity. That is why kg m/s and N s are the same unit.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two things are asked — the unit and the dimensional formula. Write both.

steps.label: The comparison
lines: They share the same unit and the same
dimensions, because impulse IS the change
describes a state at one instant.
steps.why: Same dimensions does not always mean the same quantity (torque and work share dimensions and are different) — here they genuinely match, because one is the change in the other.
common_mistakes: Saying they are unrelated because one has "time" in it.

recall.must_convey: That impulse equals the change in momentum, so they share unit and dimensions.
accept: impulse is the change in momentum

steps.memory_tip: Momentum is the reading. Impulse is the difference between two readings.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write J = Δp. A shared unit on its own does not answer the question.

insider_note: Three things are asked and there are two marks: the unit and the dimensional formula share the first, the comparison is the second.
